label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Hello D. Bergeron, Hélène here.

You are right that people deserve a straight answer, especially when they have paid in advance for their bread. I thought I was keeping a happy surprise, but after reading this thread, I can see that I mostly gave everyone something to worry about. I am sorry for that. So here is the news, without any more mystery:

**Le Pétrin Doré is not closing or moving. I bought the building.**

We signed at the notary on December 15. After being here since March 2009, I now own the building where I make your bread. This is very good news for me, and I hope it will be good news for the neighbourhood too.

First, though, let me answer the question about the carnets clearly.

**Every carnet is still valid. There is no expiry date.** If you have seven loaves left, you still have seven loaves. The $60 carnets we sold in October are for 12 loaves, exactly as promised. We sold 214 of them, and I intend to honour every one. A temporary closure for work does not change that.

Also, if anyone would rather have their money back, please come and see me at the bakery. I will refund what you have left on your carnet, no questions asked. You do not have to argue your case or feel uncomfortable asking.

Every carnet holder can also have one free croissant in January, with my thanks. You supported us by buying your bread ahead of time, and I am grateful for that.

I will be honest: reading the word “scam” hurt. I have spent nearly 17 years on this corner, and many of the people holding those carnets are people I see every week. But I understand that you could not know what I had not told you. The answer is to explain myself, not to get angry with my neighbours.

**We will be closed from January 4 through January 18 for work, and we will reopen on Tuesday, January 19, at 7 a.m.**

It is not a farewell, and it is not two weeks of vacation either, although Priya is right that bakers could sometimes use one!

We are getting a new four-deck oven from a supplier in Laval. Our old oven dates from 1998 and has broken down three times this year. Some of you have already met me on the mornings when it decided not to cooperate. I am looking forward to making bread without wondering what it will do next.

We are also taking over the space at the back, the old storage area for the dépanneur. There will be six small tables. Finally, you will be able to sit down. It is not a huge expansion, but for this little bakery it is something I have wanted for a long time.

About the building sale: Marc-Antoine, your cousin was half right. The building was sold — to me! Not to someone putting in condos, a bank or a vape shop. The bakery is staying a bakery.

And I want to be just as clear about the people living upstairs. **The three apartments will remain rented, with the same tenants and the same rent.** I have given the tenants that promise in writing. Their homes are not part of some surprise renovation plan. I want them to feel secure upstairs, just as I am happy to finally feel secure downstairs.

M. Ferland, who owned the building, is 81 and is retiring to Sherbrooke to be near his daughter. He offered to sell it to me before offering it to anyone else. That was a very generous chance to give me.

He has been coming in every morning for his baguette, “pas trop cuite,” for 17 years. At the notary, he cried a little. It was an emotional day for both of us. This building has been part of his life for a long time, and it has become a very big part of mine. I had wanted to tell you all that story with the new oven ready and the tables in place. I see now that I should have told you sooner.

As for the sign, my nephew Thomas wrote it at six in the morning. “Grande nouvelle bientôt” was his idea, and I said yes without thinking about how it would look beside a two-week closure notice. Please do not blame him. I am the owner, and I approved the sign. We meant good news, not a guessing game about whether your bakery was disappearing.

The shelves looking empty on the 28th were not a sign of us packing up, either. We had sold everything for Christmas Eve, including 400 bûches. It was Christmas baking, not a closing-down sale.

I understand why people worry. Mile End has lost enough small shops that a notice on a familiar door can make people expect the worst. I should have remembered that before trying to keep a surprise.

Priya, thank you for your kind words, and thank you to everyone who defended us or simply hoped there was a good explanation. It means a lot to know that people care whether we stay.

**Please come celebrate with us on Saturday, January 23.** We will already be back to our regular baking from Tuesday the 19th, but Saturday will be our chance to mark the reopening together. There will be free coffee and a piece of the new bread for everyone. Carnet holders, neighbours, upstairs tenants, people who worried, people who defended us — you are all welcome.

D. Bergeron, thank you for asking me directly. You were right to ask for an answer before January 4. I hope this puts everyone’s mind at ease.

We are staying. Now I just have to get through the work and learn the new oven.

Hélène  
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré  
5 rue Fairmount
